why do people have different accents
why do people from same country have different accents
why do people have distinct accents even if they grew up in same country
a: People develop distinct accents based on a combination of factors including geographic region, social group, age, and exposure to other speakers. Accents are shaped by the specific sounds (phonemes), intonation patterns, and speech rhythms of the language varieties spoken in a person's community during childhood. Key factors include: geographic isolation (mountain ranges, rivers, and distance historically limited contact between communities, allowing speech patterns to diverge); settlement history (areas settled by different immigrant groups retain linguistic features from those languages); social class and education (different social groups develop distinct speech patterns as markers of identity); the founder effect (the first settlers of an area establish a linguistic baseline that later generations inherit); and the principle of language change (all living languages constantly change, and without modern mass media, different regions naturally develop different pronunciations). Even within the same country, regions can have dramatically different accents due to historical settlement patterns, trade routes, and cultural exchange. The study of these geographic linguistic variations is called dialectology or geolinguistics.
